steps.text: Peel and thinly slice the onions into uniform rounds or half-moons.
Heat 15g of olive oil in a pan over medium-low heat. Add onions and a pinch of salt, cooking for 25-30 minutes, stirring occasionally until deep golden brown and jammy.
Drain and rinse the chickpeas. Peel the garlic cloves and juice the lemon.
Place chickpeas, tahini, garlic, lemon juice, and salt in a food processor. Blitz until thick, then slowly drizzle in 30g of olive oil while processing until the hummus is perfectly smooth.
Spoon the hummus onto a wide plate and use the back of a spoon to create a deep swirl. Top with the warm caramelized onions, a dusting of smoked paprika, fresh dill, and a final drizzle of olive oil.

title: Greek Chicken Gyros with Protein Tzatziki

steps.text: SAFETY: Wash your hands and clean the cutting board before handling raw chicken breast.
Grate the cucumber using the large holes of a box grater.
Thinly slice the onion, dice the tomatoes, and shred the lettuce into fine ribbons.
Cut the chicken breast into bite-sized strips or 2cm cubes for even cooking.
Place the grated cucumber in a clean kitchen towel and squeeze firmly to remove as much moisture as possible.
Lightly brush the pita breads with a drop of olive oil and toast them in a dry pan over medium heat for 1 minute per side until soft and warm.
In a large bowl, whisk together the olive oil, lemon juice, dried oregano, ground cumin, garlic powder, ground onion, salt, and black pepper.
Finely mince the garlic cloves until they form a paste-like consistency.
Lay a warm pita flat and spread a generous tablespoon of tzatziki sauce down the center.
Add the chicken to the bowl, toss well to coat, cover, and marinate in the refrigerator for at least 30 minutes.
In a medium bowl, combine the Protein Yoghurt, drained cucumber, and minced garlic.
Place a handful of shredded lettuce on top of the sauce, followed by a portion of the cooked Greek chicken.
Heat a large skillet or grill pan over medium-high heat until it begins to smoke slightly.
Stir in the lemon juice, dried dill, and salt until the mixture is uniform.
Top with sliced onions and diced tomatoes.
Add the chicken strips to the hot pan and sear for 6-8 minutes, turning occasionally until golden brown and the internal temperature reaches 74°C.
Cover and refrigerate the tzatziki until ready to assemble the gyros to allow flavors to meld.
Fold the pita over the filling, wrap the bottom tightly with parchment paper or foil, and serve immediately.
Remove the chicken from the pan and let it rest on a clean plate for 3 minutes before serving.

title: Lasagna alla Bolognese with meat ragù and creamy béchamel

steps.text: Finely dice the onion, carrot, and celery. Mince the garlic cloves.
Measure out the butter, flour, and milk. Pre-heat the milk slightly in a separate pan or microwave.
Preheat the oven to 180°C and finely grate the Parmigiano-Reggiano.
Heat olive oil in a heavy-bottomed pot over medium heat and sauté the onion, carrot, and celery until softened.
Melt the unsalted butter in a medium saucepan over medium-low heat.
Lightly grease a rectangular baking dish with butter or oil.
Add the ground beef and ground pork. SAFE HANDLING: Ensure raw meat is cooked thoroughly until browned and handle raw juices with care by washing hands and tools immediately.
Whisk in the all-purpose flour to form a roux and cook for 2 minutes while stirring constantly to avoid browning.
Spread a few spoonfuls of Meat Ragù over the bottom of the dish to prevent the pasta from sticking.
Pour in the red wine to deglaze the pot, scraping up any browned bits, and simmer until the liquid is reduced by half.
Slowly add a small amount of warm milk, whisking vigorously to incorporate and remove any lumps.
Place a layer of lasagna sheets over the sauce, trimming edges if necessary to fit the dish.
Add the canned tomatoes and the beef stock cube dissolved in 100ml of hot water.
Continue adding the milk in stages, whisking continuously until the mixture is smooth and begins to thicken.
Add a layer of ragù, followed by a layer of Creamy Béchamel, and a sprinkle of Parmigiano-Reggiano.
Stir in the minced garlic, salt, and black pepper. Lower the heat and simmer gently for at least 90 minutes.
Simmer the sauce for 5-7 minutes until it reaches a velvety, coat-the-back-of-a-spoon consistency.
Repeat the layers (pasta, ragù, béchamel, cheese) until all ingredients are used, ending with a final layer of béchamel.
Check the ragù consistency; it should be thick and rich. Adjust seasoning if necessary.
Season with ground nutmeg and salt. Remove from heat.
Top generously with the remaining Parmigiano-Reggiano to create a golden crust.
Keep warm until ready to assemble the lasagna layers.
Cover the surface with plastic wrap to prevent a skin from forming as it cools slightly.
Bake in the preheated oven for 30-40 minutes until the top is bubbling and deep golden brown.
Remove from the oven and let rest for 15 minutes before slicing to ensure the layers stay intact.

title: Tacos al Pastor with Marinated Pork and Pineapple

steps.text: Remove the corn tortillas from their packaging and separate them.
Remove the skin and core from the pineapple and cut into small 1cm cubes.
Thinly slice the pork shoulder into 1cm wide strips. SAFETY: Wash hands and all surfaces thoroughly after handling raw pork.
Preheat a dry flat griddle or skillet over medium-high heat.
Finely dice the white onion into a uniform brunoise.
In a large mixing bowl, whisk together the pineapple juice, white vinegar, chili powder, smoked paprika, garlic powder, onion powder, ground cumin, dried oregano, and salt.
Place a tortilla on the hot surface for approximately 30 seconds until it begins to puff slightly.
Wash the cilantro thoroughly, pat dry, and roughly chop both the leaves and tender stems.
Submerge the pork strips into the marinade, cover, and refrigerate for at least 1-2 hours to allow the enzymes to tenderize the meat.
Flip the tortilla and heat the other side for 20-30 seconds until warm and pliable.
Cut the limes into eighths to create serving wedges.
Heat a heavy cast-iron skillet over medium-high heat with a teaspoon of oil until shimmering.
Stack the warmed tortillas inside a clean kitchen towel or tortilla warmer to maintain heat and moisture.
Optional: Quickly toss the pineapple chunks in the pan used for the pork for 2 minutes to caramelize the sugars.
Sear the pork in small batches to avoid crowding the pan, cooking for 3-4 minutes per side until deeply charred on the edges.
Combine the diced onion and chopped cilantro in a small bowl to create a fresh taco relish.
Verify the pork has reached an internal temperature of 63°C before removing from heat.
Let the meat rest for 5 minutes, then roughly chop into small bite-sized pieces for taco filling.
Set out the pineapple, lime wedges, and onion-cilantro mix in separate serving dishes for custom assembly.

title: Enchiladas Verdes with Chicken and Queso Fresco

steps.text: Roughly chop the onion and peel the garlic cloves.
SAFETY: Pat the chicken breasts dry with paper towels and wash hands immediately after handling raw meat.
Preheat your oven to 180°C and lightly grease a 9x13 inch baking dish.
Remove the stems and seeds from the chili peppers to manage heat levels.
Season the chicken thoroughly with cumin, chili powder, garlic powder, and ground onion.
Flash-fry the tortillas in a dry pan for 15 seconds per side to make them pliable.
In a pot of boiling water, simmer the onion, garlic, and chili peppers for 10 minutes until soft.
Heat olive oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat.
Dip each tortilla into the green sauce, then fill with a generous amount of shredded chicken.
Drain the vegetables and transfer them to a high-speed blender.
Sear the chicken for 6-8 minutes per side until the internal temperature reaches 74°C.
Roll the tortillas tightly and place them seam-side down in the baking dish.
Add the fresh cilantro, lime juice, and salt to the blender jar.
Remove the chicken from the heat and allow it to rest for 5 minutes.
Pour the remaining green sauce over the rolls and sprinkle with half of the crumbled feta.
Pulse until the sauce is smooth and emulsified; if too thick, add 15ml of water.
Using two forks, shred the chicken into thin strips.
Bake for 15-20 minutes until the sauce is bubbling and the edges are slightly golden.
Keep the sauce warm in a small saucepan over low heat until assembly.
Toss the shredded meat with 30ml of the green sauce to keep it moist.
Top with shredded lettuce, a drizzle of sour cream, and the remaining feta before serving hot.
Divide the chilled ground beef into two equal 200g portions.
Slice the brioche buns horizontally and slice the Roma tomatoes into thin uniform rounds.
Form each portion into a patty about 10cm in diameter, slightly wider than your brioche bun.
Rinse the lettuce leaves under cold water and pat them completely dry using a kitchen towel.
Press a small dimple into the center of each patty with your thumb to prevent shrinking and bulging during cooking.
Spread softened butter onto the cut sides of the brioche bun halves.
In a small bowl, whisk together the garlic powder, onion powder, salt, and black pepper.
Place the buns in a separate skillet over medium heat and toast for 1-2 minutes until golden and crisp.
Season the exterior of both patties generously on both sides with the spice mixture.
During the final minute of cooking the patties, place cheddar slices on top and cover the pan to melt the cheese.
Heat a cast-iron skillet over high heat. SAFETY: Wash your hands and all surfaces that contacted raw meat thoroughly with soap.
Lay the bottom toasted bun on a plate and place a piece of lettuce followed by the tomato slices.
Place patties in the hot pan and sear for 4 minutes until a dark brown crust forms, then flip.
Carefully place the cheesed beef patty onto the tomatoes and top with the pickled cucumber slices.
Remove the patties from the heat and let them rest for 2 minutes to allow the juices to redistribute.
Finish by placing the top bun over the pickles and serve immediately while hot.

title: Buffalo Wings with Spicy Cayenne Hot Sauce

steps.text: Pat the chicken wings completely dry with paper towels; safety: ensure raw poultry is handled carefully and surfaces are sanitized afterward.
Melt the butter in a small saucepan over medium-low heat until completely liquid.
In a large bowl, whisk together the cornstarch, salt, and ground black pepper.
Whisk in the cayenne pepper, chili powder, garlic powder, and ground onion, stirring for 1 minute to toast the spices.
Toss the dried wings in the cornstarch mixture until they are thinly and evenly coated, shaking off any excess powder.
Pour in the white vinegar and add a teaspoon of salt, whisking vigorously to emulsify the fat and liquid.
Heat deep-frying oil in a heavy pot or deep fryer to 190°C.
Simmer the sauce gently on low heat for 5 minutes until it thickens slightly and develops a glossy sheen.
Fry the wings in small batches for 10-12 minutes until the skin is golden brown and very crispy.
Place the hot fried wings in a large stainless steel bowl and pour the warm sauce over them.
Ensure the internal temperature of the wings reaches 74°C for safety.
Toss the wings until every piece is thoroughly glazed and serve immediately.
Remove wings from the oil and drain on a wire rack for 2 minutes to maintain crispiness.

title: Butter Chicken with Tandoori-Grilled Chicken and Silky Tomato-Butter Sauce

steps.text: Mince the garlic and combine it in a bowl with plain yogurt, lemon juice, ginger, cumin, coriander, turmeric, salt, and cayenne pepper.
Finely dice the onion and set aside. If the canned tomatoes are whole, pulse them in a blender until perfectly smooth.
Cut the chicken breast into 3cm cubes. Ensure all pieces are uniform for even grilling.
In a large heavy-bottomed pan, melt 40g of the butter over medium heat.
Toss the chicken cubes in the tandoori marinade until well coated. Cover and refrigerate for at least 30 minutes.
Add the diced onions and sauté for 6-8 minutes until they are soft and starting to turn golden.
SAFETY: Thoroughly wash your hands, utensils, and any surfaces that came into contact with raw chicken.
Stir in the cinnamon, cardamom, and cloves. Toast the spices in the butter for 60 seconds until fragrant.
Preheat your oven grill or barbecue to 220°C.
Pour in the tomato puree and add the sugar. Simmer gently for 15-20 minutes, stirring occasionally, until the sauce reduces and darkens.
Thread chicken onto skewers or place on a wire rack over a baking sheet. Grill for 12-15 minutes, flipping once, until charred on the edges and cooked to an internal temperature of 75°C.
Lower the heat and stir in the heavy cream and the remaining 40g of butter. Mix until the sauce is silky and emulsified.
Remove the chicken from skewers and set aside to be incorporated into the sauce.
Add the grilled Tandoori Chicken pieces into the sauce. Simmer for an additional 5 minutes to let the flavors meld.
Rub the dried fenugreek leaves between your palms to release the oils and sprinkle over the hot butter chicken before serving.

title: Rotisserie-Style Chicken Gyros with Homemade Tzatziki

steps.text: Flag: Raw Meat Handling. Wash hands and surfaces after contact. Slice the chicken breasts into very thin 1cm wide strips.
Grate the cucumber using a box grater. Wrap the pulp in a clean kitchen towel and squeeze out all excess moisture.
Lightly brush both sides of each pita bread with olive oil.
Wash the Roma tomatoes and chop them into uniform cubes.
In a large bowl, whisk together the olive oil, lemon juice, oregano, thyme, basil, onion powder, garlic powder, salt, and pepper.
Mince the garlic cloves and finely chop the fresh dill.
Heat a large skillet over medium-high heat.
Peel the red onion and slice it into thin half-moons for a milder bite.
Toss the chicken strips in the marinade until fully coated, cover, and refrigerate for 30 minutes.
In a small bowl, blend the Greek yogurt with the squeezed cucumber, garlic, lemon juice, and dill.
Toast each pita for 1 minute per side until they are soft, warm, and have light golden spots.
Arrange the tomatoes and onions on a platter to be added to the gyros during final assembly.
Preheat the oven to 200°C. Place a wire roasting rack over a foil-lined baking sheet.
Season with a pinch of salt to taste and chill in the refrigerator until ready for use.
Stack the pitas and wrap them in a clean towel to keep them soft and steam slightly before serving.
Arrange the marinated chicken strips in a single layer on the rack to allow air circulation, simulating a rotisserie environment.
Roast for 20-25 minutes, or until the chicken reaches 74°C internal temperature and the edges are slightly charred.
Remove from the oven and let the meat rest for 5 minutes before assembling the gyros.
Clean the shrimps and scampi, leaving the tails on if preferred, and cut the chicken thighs into 3cm bite-sized chunks.
Finely dice the onion, mince the garlic cloves, and core and chop the tomatoes. Trim the ends of the green beans and cut into small pieces.
Finely chop the fresh parsley and cut the lemon into six uniform wedges for the final garnish.
In a separate pot, dissolve the chicken bouillon cubes in boiling water and add the saffron threads and turmeric to infuse the liquid.
In a small bowl, toss the chicken pieces with half of the smoked paprika, salt, and black pepper until evenly coated.
Using the same paella pan, sauté the onion and green beans over medium heat until the onion becomes translucent.
Heat 15ml of olive oil in a wide paella pan or large flat-bottomed skillet over medium-high heat.
Stir in the minced garlic and chopped tomatoes, cooking until the tomatoes break down into a thick, concentrated sofrito paste.
[SAFETY] Add the chicken pieces to the pan and sear until golden brown and fully cooked through (about 6-8 minutes), then remove and set aside.
Add the white rice to the pan and stir for 2 minutes to toast the grains and coat them thoroughly in the vegetable oil mixture.
[SAFETY] Add the remaining olive oil to the pan and sear the shrimps and scampi until they turn opaque and pink (2-3 minutes), then set aside.
Pour in the hot saffron-infused bouillon; spread the rice evenly across the pan but do not stir it again to ensure the 'socarrat' crust develops.
Keep the seared proteins on a warm plate covered loosely with foil while you prepare the rice base.
Simmer the rice on low heat for 15-18 minutes until most of the liquid is absorbed and the grains are tender.
Arrange the chicken, shrimps, and scampi on top of the cooked rice, garnish with lemon wedges and parsley, and rest for 5 minutes.

title: Loaded Baked Potato Soup with Crispy Skin Dippers

steps.text: Prick potatoes with a fork and coat in oil, salt, and pepper. Bake at 200°C for 1 hour or until soft.
Place the hollowed-out potato skins on a baking tray.
Dice the crispy bacon and finely chop the fresh chives.
In a large pot, fry bacon slices until crispy. Remove the bacon and set aside, leaving the fat in the pot.
Drizzle with olive oil and season with salt and pepper. Bake at the oven's highest temperature for 5 minutes until very crispy.
Ladle soup into bowls. Top with extra cheddar, chopped bacon, a dollollop of sour cream, and chives. Serve with the skin dippers.
Add celery, onion, and garlic to the rendered bacon fat. Sauté over medium heat until softened.
Slice cooked potatoes, scoop out the centers, and add the potato flesh to the soup pot.
Pour in chicken stock and half of the milk. Use an immersion blender to blitz until smooth.
Stir in heavy cream and season with salt and pepper. Simmer gently.
Turn off the heat and stir in the grated cheddar. Use the remaining milk to adjust the soup to your desired consistency.

title: Rotisserie-Style Chicken Gyros with Homemade Tzatziki

steps.text: SAFETY: Wash hands before and after handling raw poultry. Slice chicken thighs into thin, 1cm strips.
Grate the cucumber using a box grater and place in a clean kitchen towel; squeeze forcefully to remove all liquid.
Thinly shred the lettuce and slice the tomatoes and onions into thin rounds or half-moons.
In a large mixing bowl, combine the yoghurt, lemon juice, olive oil, garlic powder, ground onion, oregano, cumin, and paprika.
Mince the fresh garlic and finely chop the dill leaves.
Heat a dry skillet over medium-high heat and warm each pita bread for about 45 seconds per side until soft and pliable.
Add the chicken to the marinade, ensure every piece is coated, and refrigerate for 30 minutes.
Whisk the yoghurt with the garlic, dill, and lemon juice until smooth.
Spread 2 tablespoons of tzatziki in the center of a warm pita.
Preheat your oven to 200°C and line a baking sheet with parchment paper.
Fold in the dry cucumber shreds and refrigerate until the chicken is ready.
Top with a handful of chicken, lettuce, tomatoes, and onions; roll tightly and serve immediately.
Spread the chicken in a tight single layer and roast for 20-25 minutes until deep brown and slightly charred at the edges.
Let the chicken rest for 5 minutes, then roughly chop it to create varying textures.
Thinly slice the onion and tomato. Wash the lettuce leaves and pat dry with paper towels.
Finely mince the dill pickles until they reach a relish-like consistency.
Divide the ground beef into two equal portions and form into circular patties about 2cm thick. Create a small dimple in the center of each patty with your thumb to prevent bulging during cooking.
In a small mixing bowl, combine the mayonnaise, ketchup, and mustard.
Season both sides of the patties generously with salt, ground black pepper, garlic powder, and ground onion powder. **CAUTION: Wash your hands thoroughly after handling raw beef.**
Add the minced pickles to the bowl and stir until the mixture is fully emulsified and uniform in color.
Heat a large skillet over medium-high heat. Spread butter onto the cut sides of the brioche buns and toast them in the skillet until golden brown, then remove and set aside.
Taste and adjust seasoning if necessary, then set aside in the refrigerator until ready to assemble.
In the same skillet, place the beef patties. Sear for 3-4 minutes on the first side without moving them to develop a deep crust.
Flip the patties and immediately top each with a slice of cheddar cheese. Cover the skillet with a lid for 1-2 minutes to melt the cheese until the internal temperature of the meat reaches 71°C.
Spread a generous layer of Burger Sauce on the bottom half of the toasted brioche buns.
Layer the lettuce, the cheesy beef patty, sliced tomatoes, and onions. Top with the remaining bun half and serve immediately.
Remove the bones from the pork neck steaks and rinse the meat thoroughly to remove any bone fragments. Finely chop the shallots, garlic, and ginger.
In a large pot, melt the brown sugar with 1 tablespoon of water over medium-high heat until it turns into a dark caramel.
Add the chopped shallots, garlic, and ginger to the caramel and stir to combine.
Add the pork pieces to the pot. Handle raw meat with care and wash hands after contact.
Pour in the coconut milk and add the white pepper and fish sauce. Bring the mixture to a boil on high heat.
Reduce the heat to medium and let the pot simmer uncovered for 1.5 to 2 hours. Stir occasionally until the liquid evaporates and the sugar begins to caramelize around the meat.
While the pork is simmering, cook the jasmine rice according to package instructions.
Once the liquid is reduced and the meat is tender enough to fall apart, continue to cook and brown the meat in its own rendered fat for another 20-30 minutes, stirring to prevent burning.
Finely slice the spring onions and chili peppers. Roughly chop the cilantro.
Serve the sticky caramelized pork over a bed of jasmine rice. Garnish with spring onions, cilantro, and chili. Squeeze fresh lime juice over the top before eating.
Preheat your oven to 200 Celsius and line a large baking sheet with parchment paper to prevent the honey from sticking.
Wash and peel the carrots; if they are thick, slice them in half lengthwise to ensure even roasting.
In a small mixing bowl, whisk together the honey, olive oil, salt, black pepper, and half of the fresh thyme leaves.
Place the prepared carrots onto the baking sheet and pour the honey-thyme mixture over them.
Use your hands or a spatula to toss the carrots thoroughly until every piece is generously coated in the glaze.
Spread the carrots out into a single layer and roast in the oven for 25 to 30 minutes, turning them halfway through with tongs.
Check for tenderness with a fork; the edges should be slightly caramelized and browned when finished.
Transfer the roasted carrots to a serving platter and garnish with the remaining fresh thyme for a vibrant finish.
